q1_issues.issue: The specificational copula 'are not the ones establishing dictatorships' (a definite-description predicate containing a reduced relative) is flattened into a bare two-kind relational generic, dropping the identificational/exhaustive force the sentence's contrast carries — the text denies that dictators are THE ones who do it, not merely that dictators establish dictatorships.
'the herds' is a definite plural, which the instruction set says picks out specific things and takes a group witness and never a kind slot, yet it is encoded as the bare kind symbol herd.

q2_gaps: identity / specificational copula 'X is (not) the one(s) who V' — the categorical section covers only 'X is a/an N' class membership and 'X is ADJ', and the cleft section covers only it-clefts and 'what ... was ...' pseudo-clefts, so a definite-description predicate identifying the subject (and its negation) has no defined encoding
copular VP-ellipsis ('the herds are' = 'the herds are the ones establishing dictatorships') — ellipsis reconstruction is mentioned only for focus particles ('Ana did too')
negation of a kind-level relational generic: strength 0.0 on the opaque kind relation is not stated anywhere as the negation form for that construct
notes: Establish is licensed as an open-class kind-relation head, and the lemmatization and the 0.9 kind-characterization strength follow the striking-and-relational-generics rules; the doubt is about the ROUTE (kind relation vs. an identificational construction), not the head. No connective atom for the bare comma juxtaposition is correct.
